title: Idempotent plan guard and lightweight overlay manifests for networking
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Frequent accidental replacements and noisy plans when applying Terraform for VPC/subnet/NAT changes across environments. We have recurring operational overhead where on-call or infra engineers must triage large plans because provider upgrade quirks or overlay inconsistencies create unintended drifts. Goal: Reduce blast radius of Terraform network changes by introducing a pre-apply idempotent plan guard and a lightweight overlay manifest model that cleanly separates core, shared networking primitives from ephemeral/overlay resources. The plan guard enforces safety thresholds and meaningful diffs, while overlay manifests let teams declare short-lived add-ons without contaminating core state.
motivation: Make network infra changes predictable and auditable, speed up safe rollouts of provider upgrades, and reduce incident risk from unintended resource replacements. This also reduces Terraform plan noise for the Dedicated and Private deployment setups where network churn is costly.
approach: 1) Define an overlay manifest schema (YAML) that maps to terraform modules and marks resources as core | overlay | ephemeral. 2) Implement a pre-apply CI step (plan-guard) that parses 'terraform plan -out' and rejects applies when destructive changes exceed thresholds or when a core resource diff lacks an accompanying migration justification. 3) Add feature-flagged provider pins and a migration tolerance mode to allow gradual provider upgrades per workspace. 4) Migrate 3 staging workspaces to overlays and validate with integration tests. 5) Document operational runbook and add alerting for rejected plans.
migration_steps: Design overlay manifest schema and publish spec in Confluence (docs/infra/overlay-spec).
Create a lightweight CLI that composes overlay manifests into module inputs and runs terraform plan -out in CI.
Implement plan-guard: parse plan JSON, compute drift metrics, enforce thresholds (default reject if >5% resources are replaced or more than 1 core replacement).
Add provider pinning matrix and migration-tolerance mode in CI to allow staged provider upgrades per workspace.
Pilot: convert staging network-{east,west,eu} workspaces to overlay manifests and run 2 weeks of dry-run-only CI checks.
Rollout: enable plan-guard blocking for staging, then progressively enable for prod with a 48h operator approval window for rejected plans.
Post-migration: remove temporary migration-tolerance flags after provider upgrade completes and stability is observed for 2 weeks.
Publish runbook and dashboards tracking plan rejections, blocked applies, and unexpected replacements.
acceptance_criteria: Plan-guard CI step runs for all network workspace applies and blocks applies that exceed thresholds.
Overlay manifest spec documented and adopted by at least 3 staging workspaces.
Provider upgrade performed in a migration-tolerance mode without causing unintended core resource replacements.
Operational runbook published with clear operator approval flow for blocked plans.
Reduction in noisy plan tickets: target 50% fewer manual plan triage incidents for networking stacks over 8 weeks.
Integration tests covering overlay composition and plan-guard behavior added to infra CI and green for staging workspaces.
risks: False positives: plan-guard may block legitimate migrations if thresholds are too tight; we'll mitigate by pilot tuning and an operator approval bypass.
Complexity: overlay manifests add an abstraction layer; need good docs and examples to prevent misuse.
Compatibility: older provider versions may not produce plan JSON fields expected by our parser; include compatibility shims and a fallback non-blocking mode.
Migration overhead: initial conversion of workspaces will require focused engineering time and coordination with owners.
Edge cases: cross-workspace references and state import scenarios require explicit handling in the CLI and runbook.
Operational latency: blocking applies may delay urgent fixes; operator approval window must be pragmatic (48h default, with emergency bypass).
Security: the plan-guard runner must not leak sensitive outputs; run in private CI runners and restrict logs.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Spec sign-off and prototype plan-guard on a playground workspace.
Week 1: Pilot overlay manifests on staging-east and staging-eu (dry-run mode).
Week 2: Tune thresholds based on observed plan metrics and implement operator approval flow.
Week 3: Enable blocking mode for staging; onboard infra and platform teams.
Week 4-6: Gradual rollout to production workspaces with provider migration-tolerance flags.
Week 7+: Remove migration flags and bake-in plan-guard as standard pre-apply gate.
